Doc 3
The system will observe every actor, input, and action across the estate and the AI it runs, with no path by which any of the three reaches the estate or a model outside that observation.
NIST SP 800-53 SI-4 (System Monitoring) · CSF 2.0 DE.CM-01/09
Present
Structural — held by two independent proofs (static, runtime), not a numeric bound
A3 “Totality of sight”; A6 truth-condition 1

• Macho (the eyes): observes, scores, asserts facts — no power to act
• Totality held by static + runtime proof, independently
• User can (security officer) treat “nothing reaches the estate unobserved” as a proven structural fact, not an inventory claim taken on faith
Doc 3
The system will detect the machine-speed attack, the slow play beneath every threshold, and the authorised attack that never breaks a rule — each by a distinct, named mechanism.
CC FAU_SAA.2 (profile-based anomaly detection) · NIST SI-4(24) · CSF DE.CM-09
Present
Unruled — detection latency per shape not confirmed to a value
A3, second property; direct link named to Promise #7

• Three distinct detection paths, one per attack shape
• Intent reconciliation answers the authorised-attack shape, cross-referencing #7
• User can (security officer) trust a technically-permitted action is still caught if intent doesn't match what was declared
Doc 3
The system will route probabilistic suspicion to friction, a narrowed envelope, or the mirage, and will convict only once the actor's own conduct converts suspicion into certainty.
CC FAU_ARP.1 (calibrated automated response) · due-process analogues in automated-decision regimes
Present
Ruled mechanism — mirage entry threshold is baseline-period-deferred (Doc 3 Rulings)
A5.6; C1 (the mirage)

• Friction / narrowed envelope / mirage as the three refinement paths
• Mirage's three functions: containment, observation, conviction
• User can, if wrongly suspected, expect their own later conduct — not a score — to clear or convict them, zero false positives by construction
Doc 3
The system will act on a four-rung ladder — annotate, shape, contain, sever — bounded by a blast budget per window and a friction budget on legitimate work.
CC FAU_ARP.1 · NIST IR-4 (Incident Handling) · CSF RS.MA
Present
Ruled mechanism, values unruled — blast-budget share and friction ceiling named, not set

• Four-rung action ladder: annotate / shape / contain / sever
• Two ceilings: blast budget, friction budget
• Over-budget actions queue for human release
• User can (security officer) see only the small number of things genuinely requiring a person, each with evidence and defined choices
Doc 3
The system will make every autonomous act reversible, bounded, and witnessed — a time-to-live on every action, atomic act-and-attest, peer-countersigned.
NIST IR-4 · CC FPT_RCV (recovery, analogous)
Present
Unruled — action time-to-live named, no value confirmed

• TTL on every action
• Atomic act-and-attest, peer countersignature
• No “destroy” capability anywhere in the Watch
• User can, if wrongly caught, experience a bounded delay that expires on its own — never unbounded or irreversible harm
Doc 3
The system will write every verdict, action, attestation, and mark to the one authoritative record before the next gate is crossed, including its own mistakes.
NIST AU-2, AU-3 · CC FAU_GEN.1 · ISO/IEC 27001:2022 8.15
Present
Structural; timing qualitative — “before the next gate,” no numeric latency confirmed
A3; A5.5 “one record, two readings”

• Verdicts (signed, replayable), actions (citing the firing policy row), attestations, marks
• Watch mints its own first-party account and a second-party account of nobody else's
• User can (auditor) read the compliance record and the defence record as the same facts under two readings — they can never disagree
Doc 3

SPECIFICATION GAP — no mechanism specified. Doc 3's plain-language promise states the platform “learns from every attack it defeats”; every A5 clause on learning (A5.7, A5.8, A5.12) constrains what may NOT happen. None specifies what does update, on what evidence, at what layer.
CC FAU_SAA (would require a specified mechanism) · ISO 27001 5.27 (learning from incidents) · CSF 2.0 improvement functions
Absent → new (spec-closed, 13 Sep 2026)
Closed by Watch Learning Amendment L-2, L-4. R-15 (initial library) and R-16 (ratifier, cadence) open.

Gap between A1 (plain-language promise) and A5 (constrains learning, never specifies it)  CLOSED AT SPEC LEVEL: what updates — the certificate-requirement library; on what evidence — in-environment data points, each anchored; at what layer — deterministic gates at the verdict interface, not detector weights; under what ceremony — the Watch's own (RBM-8). Not built.
• None specified
• Not yet answerable — no mechanism exists for a user-facing guarantee
Doc 3
The system will exercise every response rail on a standing drill cadence — full loop, both engines, latencies measured — and a rail not demonstrated firing is not in force.
NIST CA-7 (Continuous Monitoring) · ISO 27001 8.16 · CC ATE (independent testing, analogous)
Present
Ruled mechanism, cadence value unruled
A5.13; A3 “self-proof on a standing cadence”

• Full-loop drills, both engines, measured latencies
• Results as receipts, assembled without human effort
• User can pull standing drill receipts proving each response mechanism actually fires, with nothing assembled by hand
Doc 3
The system will, on release from the mirage, replay the actor's mirage-period work against the real platform, or tell them plainly it did not land.
No direct security-standard analogue — nearest is adverse-action notice in automated-decision regimes (GDPR Art. 22; Kenya DPA 2019 s.35)
Present
Ruled mechanism — reconciliation mode is baseline-period-deferred
C1, “reconciliation duty”

• Automatic replay or plain notice on release
• Short expiry with automatic release on zero incrimination
• User can, if wrongly caught and routed to the mirage, be told plainly whether their work landed — never left believing a false success
Wave E · CA1-N5 (no document home yet — proposed Doc 3 Part D)
The system will restore Ledger continuity within 3,600 seconds, under independent countersign, following any continuity-affecting incident.
NIST CP-10 / IR-4 (Recovery) · ISO 27001 5.29/5.30 · CSF 2.0 RC.RP
Absent → new
Ruled — CA1-N5, RTO 3,600s, DEFAULT-class, revisable on incident evidence
Wave E ruling CA1-N5; not yet written into Doc 3 as a Watch/Ledger promise

• 3,600-second RTO
• Independent countersign on restoration
• User can trust any continuity-affecting incident is bounded to a known, ruled recovery window, not an open-ended outage
Wave E · CA1-N2 (no document home yet — proposed Doc 3 Part D)
The system will issue breach notification within 72 hours of a qualifying incident, to the parties and authorities the incident requires.
NIST IR-6 · ISO 27001 5.26 · Kenya Data Protection Act 2019 (breach notification duty) · GDPR Art. 33 (international analogue)
Absent → new
Ruled — CA1-N2, 72-hour duty
Wave E ruling CA1-N2; not yet written into Doc 3

• 72-hour notification clock
• Tied to the incident classes S-2 / S-4 detect and contain
• User can (compliance owner) trust a qualifying breach triggers notification on a ruled clock, not a judgement call made under pressure
Doc 3
The system will fail closed independent of the Watch — custody gates fail closed on their own, with or without the Watch above them.
CC FPT_FLS.1 · NIST SC-24 · IEC 61508 (safe state)
Present
Structural
A5.9, parenthetical: “Custody gates fail closed on their own, per Document 1, with or without the Watch above them”

• Custody-gate fail-closed independent of Watch liveness
• Watch silence is itself an alarm, not a fail-open trigger
• User can trust a compromised or silent Watch cannot cause a custody gate to fail open — the two failure modes are structurally independent
Doc 3
The system will never let detection hold power to act, or response hold judgement to interpret — Macho asserts facts only; Mkono executes signed policy only; one verdict is the sole interface.
CC FAU_ARP (separation of detection/response) · platform-wide “detect, never decide” doctrine
Present
Structural
A5.1; C2 (verdict seam)

• Macho / Mkono split
• Single signed, replayable, externally-versioned verdict interface
• User can (auditor) confirm detection quality was never silently tuned defensively — the detector never knew what action would follow its own verdict
Doc 3
The system will never unlock its maximum autonomous force from a signal an outsider could fabricate — only from a closed, six-member registry of unfakeable signals.
No direct security-standard analogue — borrows the assertion-boundary discipline of Solva (Doc 4), an internal cross-reference
Present
Structural; registry membership is baseline-period-deferred

• Closed six-signal registry (canary touch, attestation failure, mark hit, witness-write attempt, floor violation, mirage incrimination)
• Certainty computation has no parameter a detector's confidence can enter
• User can trust no confidence score, however high, can trigger severance alone — only an unfakeable structural signal can
Doc 3
The system will never let loss of behavioural conformance alone convict an actor — the worst it can do to an innocent actor is return them to baseline verification.
GDPR Art. 22 · Kenya Data Protection Act 2019 s.35 — legal analogues, not security-conformance standards
Present
Structural, constitutional per A5.7 — not tunable

• Conformance grants a trust discount
• Non-conformance returns to baseline only, never sole grounds past friction
• User can lose their trust discount without ever being convicted by that loss alone — the asymmetry is fixed, not configurable
Doc 3
The system will hold a ruled, deterministic floor beneath every adaptive layer, moved only by a delayed, two-signature ceremony that is itself a monitored tripwire.
NIST AC-3 (mandatory enforcement) · CC FDP_ACF · Document 0 Attribute 7 (mandatory baseline)
Present
Structural — floor values are the conservative defaults during the baseline period

• Deterministic floor beneath adaptive layers
• Two-signature, delayed-countdown ceremony to move it
• Ceremony itself monitored as a tripwire
• User can trust the floor cannot be “boiled” one degree at a time — only moved in daylight, under two names, on a countdown, with the Watch watching
Doc 3
The system will never delete — the Watch can stop anything and erase nothing; destruction remains solely the separately-authorised act specified elsewhere.
NIST AU-9 (protection of audit information) · CC FAU_STG.1
Present
Structural
A3; A5.3 “destroy does not exist in the Watch”

• No destroy capability anywhere in the Watch
• Deletion authority lives in a separate, named document/act only (Document 14)
• User can trust nothing is ever erased by the Watch's response to a threat — only a separately-authorised act can delete anything
Doc 3
The system will hold behavioural-conformance profiles as non-exportable, tenant-keyed, purpose-bound armoury — never rendered to any surface, export, or analytic, including the Watch's own console.
NIST SC-28 (protection of information at rest, analogous) — no direct standard for “never render to own console”
Present
Structural; retention posture is baseline-period-deferred

• Per-actor, tenant-keyed, non-exportable profile store
• Holds learned parameters only, never raw action history
• User can trust their own behavioural profile is never visible to scoring, pricing, or management surfaces — including to the Watch's own operators
Doc 3

The system will have its own liveness attested by a component holding no Watch credentials, will treat Watch silence itself as an alarm, and will subject its own records to a standing break-in test that must fail.
CC ADV_ARC.1 self-protection (verified, Document 0 Attribute 6) · NIST SI-4 · reference-monitor tamper-resistance generally
Present
Structural; break-in test cadence unruled
A5.9; C3 (the witness)

• External liveness attestation (no Watch credentials)
• Silence-as-alarm
• Standing break-in test against own production credentials, must fail
• User can (auditor) confirm the Watch's own tamper-resistance is measured, not asserted — a standing test actively tries to beat it and is expected to fail
Doc 3
The system will execute every task under exactly one authority's identity and scope — a task that could see like security and decide like governance is unrepresentable, not merely forbidden.
NIST AC-6 (least privilege / separation of duties, analogous) · CC FDP_ACC (separation of security policies)
Present
Structural — unrepresentable, not policy-enforced
A5.10; A5.11 “peer, not subordinate”; cross-referenced to #26's single-crossing/no-side-door doctrine

• One-task-one-identity, structurally unrepresentable dual-hatting
• Watch authors its own policy; rules service administers ceremony without editorial power
• User can (auditor) confirm no credential spans both the Watch's authority and governance's authority — the surface doesn't exist to be compromised
Doc 3
The system will let the mirage deceive outward only — every mirage interaction writes truthfully marked records, and mirage state shares no store with production.
MITRE Engage (deception framework, closest analogue, no formal conformance standard) · NIST SI-4 deception guidance (informal)
Present
Structural — mirage entry threshold is baseline-period-deferred (cross-ref S-3)
A5.5 “the record never lies inward”; C1 (the mirage)

• Mirage renders outward deception only
• Truthfully-marked records regardless of what's shown to the suspect
• No shared store with production — bleed unrepresentable
• User can (auditor) trust the platform's deliberate deception layer never corrupts its own truthful record — the lie never reaches inward
Doc 3 (proposed A5.15) · DAP-33

The system will inspect what leaves, not only who sends it — every output leaving a component boundary is checked for controlled-unit content and tagged ADVISORY where it recommends, ranks, proposes, or evaluates an action.

Solva assertion floor (Doc 4) as internal precedent for output gating · DLP practice at the component boundary — no direct security-conformance standard for output-content gating as a security function
Absent → new
Ruled — reproduction threshold and probe design are R-8 (DEFAULT-class, conservative, revised on evidence)
Security Amendments W-1; gate sits on the deterministic side of the verdict seam

• Deterministic output gate at every component boundary
• Reproduction probe against the producing job's read set
• ADVISORY tag carrying producer identity, content hash, units drawn on
• Refusal with reason, never a redacted output

• User can (auditor) confirm no permitted output carried controlled content past the boundary
• User can (human recipient) see that what they received is advice, from whom, drawing on what — before acting on it
Document 0 Attribute 3 · Doc 3 (proposed A5.18) · DAP-34
The system will treat a coalition as one actor — cumulative conduct across principals sharing a party, a mandate lineage, or a detected coordination signature is evaluated jointly, not per principal.
Sybil resistance (Douceur 2002) · Byzantine fault tolerance — established distributed-systems frames; no security-conformance standard names coalition-as-principal
Absent → new
Structural for shared-party and shared-lineage membership; coordination-signature threshold is R-11 — inferred, friction-only under A5.2
Security Amendments W-4; coalition is a connected component of the admission graph

• Coalition graph from DAP-1/DAP-2 admission records
• Joint cumulative history and slow-play evaluation
• Three membership classes: party, lineage (structural), coordination signature (inferred)

• User can (estate owner) see every principal evaluated jointly with a given party, and every inferred coalition labelled as suspicion
• User can (external party) know at admission that its principals are evaluated jointly
Doc 3 (proposed A5.17)

The system will hold the raiser of a finding to the same conformance as its target — a finding is conduct; the friction it causes is charged to the raiser's budget, not the target's; a finding not borne out accrues drift on the raiser; and no agent-raised finding, at any count, is an input to severance.
A5.2 (findings already excluded from the severance registry) · A5.14 (friction budget) · BFT source weighting — no direct conformance standard
Absent → new
Structural — A5.2's registry unchanged; friction debit follows A5.14's existing budget
Security Amendments W-3; two finding classes, D (deterministic) and A (advisory), never merged

• Class D vs Class A findings
• Lineage collapse — N findings from one coalition count as one
• Friction debited to raiser
• Drift on raiser when a finding is not borne out

• User can (legitimate actor) not be harassed into friction by manufactured findings without the raiser paying for it
• User can (auditor) see who raised what, what it cost, and whether it was borne out
DAP-35, DAP-36 · Document 0 Attribute 7 (new mandatory baseline)

The system will bound what the estate releases in total — across all parties, all operations, all time — so that no combination of parties can reconstruct what none of them is entitled to. Breaching the bound is a floor violation, severance-eligible without inference.
Differential privacy (Dwork et al. 2006) · NIST SP 800-188 (2023) — de-identification, privacy budgets, composition · DP-SGD (Abadi et al. 2016) for training
Absent → new
Ruled — the budget itself is R-7; per-run (ε, δ) is R-9. The floor never learns (A5.8)
Security Amendments W-7, W-8; the amendment that converts coalition prevention from detection into a ruling

• Estate-level release accumulator, debited per metered event before return
• Differential-privacy budget composed across releases
• DP-SGD default for every fine-tune
• Floor violation on breach — one of the six unfakeable signals
• Remaining budget never disclosed to parties

• User can (estate owner) set and see the estate's total exposure as a single number, and see consumption against it
• User can (external party) know that the estate's releases are bounded — and never see the remaining budget
DAP-37, DAP-38 · Pruning & Unlearning Amendment (9 Sep 2026)

The system will remove a unit's influence from every artefact that carried it when the right to that unit ends — by re-derivation or recall, findable by registry query, with the release budget's prior consumption left unrefunded.
SISA (Bourtoule et al. 2021) · Certified Data Removal (Guo et al. 2020) · Kenya DPA 2019 s.40 · GDPR Art. 17 — extends CA1-N3's already-ruled model-flagging answer to DAP-governed artefacts
Absent → new
Ruled where sharded (SISA); R-12 open for the unsharded, uneconomic-retrain case
Pruning & Unlearning Amendment T-3, T-4; generalises CA1-N3 (already ruled) to artefacts DAP now governs

• Registry query finds every artefact citing a withdrawn unit (RBM-20)
• Re-derivation excludes the unit, re-passes MOAC and DAP-31 as a new artefact
• Recall withdraws the registry entry and notifies the receiving party
• Release-budget consumption is not refunded on unlearning

• User can (contributor) trust that withdrawing consent reaches every artefact trained on their data, not only the source record
• User can (external party) be notified if an artefact they hold is recalled, rather than silently invalidated
V-1–V-4 · Serving Integrity Amendment (13 Sep 2026)
The system will serve exactly the model it registered — pressure may make it slower, never different — and will say on the record which engine, its own or a provider's, produced every answer.
A5.8 (no silent recalibration, rules layer) · SEC-1/SEC-2 load-time integrity pattern · FDP_ACC.1 form (SFP-8) · invariant generalised from the Colibri engine's stated design rule (Apache 2.0)
Absent → new
R-13 (validation cadence, DEFAULT-class) open; floor explicitly not imposable on the frontier gateway tier — receipt records the boundary instead (V-4)
Serving Integrity Amendment V-1 (A20.15, SFP-8), V-2 (gate conformance), V-4 (receipt fields); TCB entry and failure-posture row per its §6

• Artefact hash verified against the register before first token
• Token-exact reproduction check, on demand and on schedule
• Gates (DAP-31/32, MOAC) assert path conformance before their verdict counts
• Non-conforming path refuses to serve — fail-closed

• User can (estate owner) trust that the model tested is the model running, under any load
• User can (any consumer) see on the receipt whether an answer came from the platform's own serving or a frontier provider's
L-1–L-4 · Watch Learning Amendment (13 Sep 2026)

The system will never act on a verdict it cannot evidence — every Watch action carries a certificate a human can read, and every behaviour it learns to recognise entered its vocabulary through ceremony, not through silent training.

Doc 3 A2, A5.2 (no confidence parameter) · Doc 4 A2/A5.5 assertion floor, applied to verdicts · RBM-8 (system-TCB ceremony) · CIF single-experiment principle (BR-9.2) · EU AI Act Art. 14(c), now structurally evidenced
Absent → new
R-15 (initial certificate library seed) and R-16 (ratifying role, research-queue cadence) open; severance still unlocks only from A5.2's registry — a certificate never does

Watch Learning Amendment L-1 (A5.19 certificate on the verdict), L-2 (A5.20 + RBM-23 requirements as TCB-tier rules), L-3 (A5.21 + DAP-32+ + AC-15 mirage as certificate ground), L-4 (A5.22 + AC-16 research loop)

• Every verdict carries {requirement_id, data_points, observation_refs}; schema has no confidence field
• Requirements enter force only through the Watch's ceremony; provenance links to originating incidents
• Mirage provokes certified behaviours pre-admission; failure withholds scope
• Unsure cases enter a research queue: CIF proposes, Solva grounds, a human ratifies

• User can (overseer) read what a verdict saw, not just how sure the detector was
• User can (owner) see exactly which incidents taught the Watch each behaviour it now recognises
• User can (contained party) know that no action was taken against it without evidence on the record
L-5 · Watch Learning Amendment (13 Sep 2026)
The system will admit no new class of action into the world without ceremony on the record — every action names the admission it acts under, and no learner ratifies its own.

DAP-37 (new hash = new artefact) · BR-9.2 (CIF acceptance point) · AC-1/AC-2 · RBM-2/RBM-8 · Instrumental convergence (Omohundro 2008, Bostrom 2012): gate exercise where observable, not acquisition where it isn't
Absent → new
R-17 (class granularity, initial register) open. Learning itself is deliberately ungoverned; exercise is governed at the seams. AC-1's four ceilings are not admissible classes under any ceremony.

Watch Learning Amendment L-5: A20.16 (capability-class register, versioned with the artefact), AC-17 (per-action citation + certificate; first exercise = foundation floor + research queue), AC-18 (learner proposes, never ratifies)

• Register stored with the artefact's registry entry; new hash inherits no admissions
• Every action cites its admitted class by lookup; ceremony once per class, never per action
• Uncited action = first exercise: reversible ladder only, data points collected, research queue
• Proposal path exists for the learner; ratification path does not

• User can (overseer) see every class of action a model or agent is admitted to, and which ceremony admitted it
• User can (owner) know a retrained version starts with no inherited admissions
• User can (deploying lab) request new capability for an agent without being able to grant it
MEM-1–MEM-11 · Memory Compaction & Preservation (memory_compaction_v1, 18 Sep 2026)
The system will make what it holds smaller without losing what it can prove — every compaction is decided by rule, receipted, anchored to its sources, and says on reload what it no longer contains.
Attribute 10 (learned proposes, deterministic decides) · Doc 4 A2/A5.5 assertion floor · B.4 Ledger standard · DAP-37 new-hash, DAP-38 erasure · SFP-8 deterministic reload · Kenya DPA 2019 s.40
Absent → new
R-19 (triggers), R-20 (retention rule set v1) open; R-21 (user-memory class, consent model) owner input — class ships disabled until ruled

memory_compaction_v1: MEM-3 retention by deterministic rule set; MEM-6 receipted compaction with loss statement; MEM-7/8 deterministic reload that states depth lost; MEM-9 erasure overrides retention; MEM-10 user memory as personal data

• Facts kept by text-hash pointer, never rewritten; receipts and refusals kept by reference
• Ledger row before the artefact is readable; source untouched if the row fails
• Reload verifies the artefact hash; refuses rather than serves best-effort
• Withdrawn units found by provenance; artefact re-derived or recalled

• User can (overseer) see exactly what a compacted context no longer contains
• User can (principal) read their own user memory and have it erased
• User can (owner) know the record was never made smaller
ENT-1–ENT-49 · The Entitlement Service (entitlement_service_v1, 20 Sep 2026)

One licence reaches every listed model the buyer's settings admit, resolved at the single chokepoint, metered on the one Ledger, with unlimited local use and no silent fallback — what the buyer sees is what was used.
A5.1 single chokepoint · DAP-21/22/23/26 metering, terms, ceilings · Doc 11 A5.4 / D-16 cascade · Doc 20 registry · PRIN-5–8 credential plane · D-17 provider posture · FE brief §2 honest display
Absent → new
R-24 (reseller agreements, counsel) gates reseller-frontier rows only; R-25–R-31 commercial and DEFAULT values open; Local and Your Keys ship without R-24

entitlement_service_v1: ENT-16/17 deterministic resolution, fail-closed; ENT-20–22 bill derived from Ledger events only; ENT-26/34 visible fallback with fixed strings; ENT-29 no token cap on local; ENT-35 keys never displayable; ENT-49 no state outside licence/row/credential/event

• Every call resolves principal → licence → row → dial → allowance before dispatch; any missing link refuses
• Allowance is recomputed from events, never a stored counter
• Exhaustion serves locally with the fixed string, never silently
• Reseller row cannot be listed before its agreement is on record

• User can see credits remaining and tokens by model, derived from the Ledger
• User can (admin) add, rotate, revoke a key in one act and never see it again
• User can (owner) change any price or rate only through ceremony, prospectively
PRIN-1–PRIN-13 · The Principal Model (principal_model_v1, 20 Sep 2026)
Every record the platform writes is attributed to an admitted principal whose identity was authenticated and propagated by construction — never to a caller-supplied string, never to a default actor.
DAP-1–5 external-party principal · DAP-13 keys per principal · DAP-21 metering attribution · Attribute 12 trust domain · Promise #32 objective freeze (mandate)
Absent → new
R-22 (rotation default), R-23 (legacy route shapes) DEFAULT-class open

principal_model_v1: PRIN-2 no self-admission; PRIN-6 credential material never readable back; PRIN-9/10 trust-domain identifier on every record, refused if absent; PRIN-11/12 actor populated only from propagated context, fail-closed on absence; PRIN-13 context read-only in flight

• A write with no principal in calling context fails closed
• The Ledger actor field is never caller-supplied
• A credential is bound to one trust domain at issuance
• Mandate is frozen at admission; change is a new admission

• User can (owner) see who did what, by admitted identity, on every record
• User can (principal) hold a credential that nobody — including the platform — can display
• User can (owner) revoke any principal in one act
CON-1–CON-31 · The Content Registry (content_registry_v1, 20 Sep 2026)

Nothing a surface says is improvised: every string has a stated purpose and a class; every number comes from a measured field; generated prose is anchored and gated; and where a surface has several true things to say, the one it says first is chosen by rule, and the reason is on record.

FE brief §0.2 DOM-bound substitution rules · FE brief §2.1 measured numbers · Doc 4 A2/A5.5 assertion floor · A5.15 output gate · A5.16 recommendation provenance · DAP-38/MEM-9 erasure · EU AI Act Art. 14(c)
Absent → new
R-32 (Generated surfaces) owner; R-33 (salience classes v1), R-34 (hold), R-35 (retention) DEFAULT-class

content_registry_v1: CON-1 no string without an entry; CON-4 honest-gap variant mandatory; CON-6 prose never supplies a number; CON-12 resolver pure, no learned parameter; CON-15–18 rule-ranked hook, no engagement signal; CON-20 salience trace receipted; CON-24 unsupported claims refused not softened; CON-25 templated text re-derived, never stored

• A number reaches a surface only as a verified dependency
• An ineligible candidate is never the hook while any eligible one exists
• No engagement or learned signal enters ranking
• A generated string that fails classing or the gate is refused, not hedged

• User can ask any slot “why this first” and see what it chose not to lead with
• User can see the anchors of any generated line
• User can (owner) change any template, prompt, or ranking only through ceremony
DQ-1–DQ-15 · Data Cleanliness (data_cleanliness_v1, 26 Sep 2026)

The platform knows, per record, which checks it passed and which it failed; no figure about cleanliness is shown without its checks; nothing that failed structural validity or carries a sentinel enters training or anchors a fact; and every source's strata reconcile to its record count.
Document 9 B3/B5 census quality strata · Targeta MOAC every-criterion rule · Doc 4 A2/A5.5 assertion floor · Execution Standard EX-9 reconciliation
Absent → new
R-38 (sentinel threshold), R-39 (fuzzy tolerance), R-40 (media thresholds) DEFAULT-class

data_cleanliness_v1: DQ-1–8 seven check families, deterministic; DQ-10 stratum a pure function of bitmap and pack; DQ-12 register reconciles or is not published; DQ-13 accuracy only against named ground truth; DQ-14 training gate as a MOAC criterion; DQ-15 Junk never anchors a fact

• Every bit maps to a named check in a versioned pack
• No merge path exists in code; merges are human acts, receipted
• Clean + Repairable + Suspect + Junk = record count, per source
• A Junk record in a manifest is refused at commission

• User can (owner) read the garbage register per source and the checks that placed each record

Security Assurance Promise Set — Legend
Scope of this set
S-1–S-34 are entirely scoped to Document 3 (the Watch). They do not cover SyniSense's Document 1 domain — stated explicitly because of the finding immediately below.
“A5.7” — a citation warning, not an error

Positional IDs (rule_criteria_spec_v1 ROC-3) are document-scoped by design: Document 1 has its own A5.7 (the trust receipt — custody status, signature, organisation-binding) and Document 3 has a separate, unrelated A5.7 (non-conformance ceiling, S-15 in this set, “never convict on non-conformance”). Both are correct within their own document. Citing “A5.7” without naming the document is how the two get conflated — caught here on a direct re-check while updating this file, not before.
G-8 and G-9 — why neither has a row here

Document 0's G-8 (Governance Architecture) concerns Document 1's A5.7, the trust receipt — outside this set's scope. Its fix lives in Security_Promise_Set_Amendments.docx, Amendment 3, and in akki_governance_architecture_v1's own G-8 entry, not as an S-row. G-9 (system-rule change control) is a Rules Service / Attribute 9 matter, not a Watch conduct promise, and likewise has no natural S-row. Neither omission is an oversight; both are stated here so the absence reads as scoped, not missed.

Standard column
The clause each promise answers to. [V]/[K]/[P] confidence not marked per-cell here; treat citations as [K] (established knowledge, stable clause reference) unless a document says otherwise.
Bound / Ruling column

Structural = no numeric bound applies. Ruled = a specific value is set (cites the ruling). Baseline-period-deferred = Doc 3's own mechanism: conservative default until a defined observation period, then set by evidence. Unruled = a bound is named in A5 text with no value confirmed — a real gap, not a placeholder.
Status colours

Green = Present, built and grounded in canon text. Blue = Absent → new, a ruled value with no document promise yet. Amber = Absent → gap, no mechanism specified anywhere. Grey = By design, composite/umbrella row.
